items.title: Jay McShann interviewed by Monk Rowe, Sarasota, Florida, April 12, 1996
items.q: every night the guy that was doing the film, Bruce Ricker, Bruce would send Joe [Turner] home with a fifth of scotch

ctx.x: What was it like doing the films? You did the “Hootie Blues” and —

Well we had a lot of fun. A lot of people came up there and got full of that mess, they’d had a little too much you know? And you’d turn and every night the guy that was doing the film, Bruce Ricker, Bruce would send Joe [Turner] home with a fifth of scotch, and another fifth to wake up on. And he’d give him a slab of ribs — and get him two slabs of ribs. One slab is to eat that night, and if he didn’t finish that he’d wake up during the night and eat the rest of it. And then wake up with a slab. A fifth and a…
And “The Last of the Blue Devils.” That was a great little film.

items.title: 52193_Jay McShann oral history interview
items.q: Bruce Ricker decided he wanted to do a film on Kansas City jazz. And then as things rocked along, he wound up calling it 'The Last of the Blue Devils.' ... we had a big band and we had other smaller groups that also appeared.

ctx.x: The other thing we didn't mention was this film which you made in Kansas City.

Oh, yes. We -- Bruce Ricker decided he wanted to do a film on Kansas City jazz. And then as things rocked along, he wound up calling it 'The Last of the Blue Devils.' That's what he called the film. And, well, we had a big band and we had other smaller groups that also appeared. Basie came down, he talked, and then he got some -- oh, some -- Basie and them were doing some things, too, you know what I mean, which was Kansas City jazz.
Yeah, it was supposed to be a sort of Kansas City jazz thing.
